materials.label: House F teacher–student tablet 3N-T 397
materials.what_audience_follows: On one House F tablet, a competent model, a student's erased copy and an older exercise on the reverse expose learning as repeated copying, correction, memorization and revision rather than simple sign recognition.
sequence: On the obverse left, a competent hand writes eleven lines from Syllable Alphabet B as a model.
On the obverse right, the student's copy is written, erased and prepared to be copied again.
On the reverse, a longer earlier passage is written as revision of previously learned material.
Across House F, comparable tablet formats let scholars reconstruct a staged curriculum while also showing that the exact order varied by school.

locators: Section 'Elementary education in House F', paras. 10–16 / pp. 45–49
Fig. 9: 3N-T 397 = UM 55-21-320, Type II teacher–student tablet
Table 1 and paras. 11–12: Type II obverse model/copy and reverse revision logic

limitations: House F is an unusually rich eighteenth-century BCE Nippur household-school context and cannot be projected back to Uruk.
Its curriculum was not a universal Mesopotamian standard; the source explicitly finds local variation.
The teacher/student attribution is inferred from relative competence and tablet format, not from named biographies.
